"A mysterious stranger, a tavern, a dungeon, and a twist. Some assembly required. Not anymore."

Roll a whole adventure for tonight's table: a villain with a plan, a patron with a secret, a trail of clues, the road, a keyed dungeon with its map, fights balanced for your party, the hoard, and how it ends. Keep the parts you like, reroll the rest, then print it and play.

How to run a rolled one-shot

A one-shot is a complete adventure in a single session (or two). This one is built in three acts: the hook in a town tavern, where a patron offers the job; the road, where the party follows the trail, travels, and meets the villain's people; and the site, a keyed dungeon with the villain waiting in the last room. Read the red "What's really going on" box first: it's the part the players never see, and everything else follows from it.

Keep, reroll, and mix

  • 🔒 Keep a part (the site and its villain, the plot, the town and patron, the road, the hoard) and 🎲 Roll New Adventure leaves it alone.
  • 🎲 on a part rerolls only that part. A new site brings a new villain, and the rest of the story uses the new name.
  • Pick a tone (heroic, horror, intrigue, comedic) for the read-aloud text, the twist, and the ending, and a length for the size of the site and the days on the road.

At the table

The three clues follow the "three clue rule": the party only needs one of them to find the site, so a failed check never stalls the game. The fights are balanced for your party's level and size, with the boss fight at the end rated High. Every monster's stat block is in the appendix, and the whole module prints on a few pages. Change anything that doesn't suit your table: the generator gives you a first draft, not a script.

Works with

Each fight opens in the Encounter builder, and the site opens in the Dungeon Generator, where you can download its battle map. Need more people for the town? Roll them in Town Square. Articles in the Gazette with a "Use This in My Campaign" box can start a one-shot of their own.
